assessment_scope: Repository-local maturity for requested agent modules. Scores measure implemented, documented, and tested UAA artifacts, not product ambition or roadmap intent.

maturity_levels.label: Missing
maturity_levels.definition: No meaningful source, tests, or active documentation for the requested module.

maturity_levels.label: Declared only
maturity_levels.definition: Named in docs or old registries, but not maintained as current tested implementation.

maturity_levels.label: Contract only
maturity_levels.definition: Typed contracts, metadata, or policy records exist, but no operating runtime behavior for the requested module.

maturity_levels.label: Validated contract
maturity_levels.definition: Contract logic has deterministic evaluators and tests, but remains review-only or no-effect.

maturity_levels.label: Constrained local runtime
maturity_levels.definition: A bounded local/dev runtime path exists and is tested, with explicit non-production authority limits.

maturity_levels.label: Operational runtime
maturity_levels.definition: The module can perform its intended runtime function in product workflows with durable integration and guardrails.

maturity_levels.label: Production ready
maturity_levels.definition: The module is hardened for production authority, external integrations, observability, recovery, and operational use.

modules.name: Agent runtime skeleton
modules.requested_definition: A starter framework that defines how the agent receives input, thinks, calls tools, stores state, and returns output.
modules.summary: UAA has a minimum kernel runner that accepts typed task requests, builds execution/context contracts, checks consent and approval, evaluates a tool request, can apply one governed local/dev file mutation, writes local recall memory, appends ledger events, and returns receipts. It is not a general agent loop and does not run model reasoning or arbitrary tools.
evidence: MinimumKernelRunner coordinates contracts, consent, tool broker, local file manager, memory store, ledger, and receipt generation.
Happy-path tests prove a bounded local/dev file write, rollback ref, world-state artifact ref, receipt, and recall-only memory record.
modules.next_checkpoint: Separate the minimum kernel from a future general Agent Runtime contract before claiming operational_runtime.

modules.name: Orchestration layer
modules.requested_definition: Coordinates the full flow across prompts, tools, memory, APIs, workflows, and sub-agents.
modules.summary: UAA has orchestration-adjacent pieces: the kernel coordinates a narrow local/dev flow, and the orchestration efficiency planner previews model-route choices. There is no single Commander or full-flow orchestrator spanning prompts, memory, workflows, APIs, and sub-agents.
evidence: OrchestrationEfficiencyPlanner deterministically previews route selection, fallback planning, cacheability effects, and approval requirements.
Layered architecture declares Layer 3 orchestration responsibilities.
gaps: No prompt-tool-memory-workflow coordinator as one module.
modules.next_checkpoint: Create a single orchestration contract that references the existing kernel, planning, tool, memory, and execution boundaries.

modules.name: Decision router
modules.requested_definition: Chooses what path to take: answer directly, call a tool, search memory, ask a human, escalate, or trigger a workflow.
modules.summary: UAA has specialized routers and decision envelopes, including model routing, truth routing, recall routing, tool broker decisions, approval decisions, and planning decisions. It does not have one top-level decision router that chooses between answer, memory, tool, human, escalation, and workflow paths.
evidence: Specialized routers make deterministic local decisions inside their own domains.
Decision envelopes are tested for model routing, recall, truth, tools, and approvals.
gaps: No unified route taxonomy for direct answer versus memory versus tool versus human versus workflow.
No single decision trace across all possible paths.
modules.next_checkpoint: Define a top-level DecisionRouter contract before implementing runtime path selection.

modules.name: Planning module
modules.requested_definition: Breaks a goal into steps, tracks progress, and updates the plan as new information appears.
modules.summary: UAA has task goal, step, dependency, plan, receipt, and review-only decision contracts with evaluator validation. It does not generate plans from vague goals or update plans dynamically during execution.
evidence: evaluate_task_plan validates goals, steps, input boundaries, dependency cycles, hidden side effects, and non-authoritative receipts.
Tests assert review-only behavior and no execution authorization.
gaps: No plan generation from natural-language goals.
modules.next_checkpoint: Add a planner input contract for explicit decomposition proposals before adding any automatic planner.

modules.name: Task decomposition module
modules.requested_definition: Turns vague user requests into concrete subtasks.
modules.summary: UAA can represent decomposed tasks as TaskPlan and TaskStep contracts, but it does not contain a decomposition engine that transforms vague requests into subtasks.
evidence: TaskPlan and TaskStep provide the structure needed to store decomposed work.
Planning tests cover safe plan structure and denial conditions.
modules.next_checkpoint: Introduce a review-only decomposition proposal record with safe input and output refs.

modules.name: Workflow engine
modules.requested_definition: Runs repeatable sequences like research, summarize, draft, review, send.
modules.summary: UAA has a multi-step execution framework that models runs, steps, dependencies, transitions, replay protection, and no-effect completion. It does not run real repeatable workflows, execute tasks, call tools for workflow steps, or send outputs.
evidence: Execution state machine validates dependencies, replay keys, transition IDs, and no-effect transitions.
Docs explicitly state the framework is not real task execution.
modules.next_checkpoint: Keep workflow maturity at validated_contract until a safe runner is separately designed and approved.

modules.name: State manager
modules.requested_definition: Tracks what the agent is currently doing, what it has already tried, and what still needs to happen.
modules.summary: UAA has structured world state, execution run state, event ledger records, and kernel result/world-state refs. These pieces track state in bounded domains, but there is no single general state manager for live agent cognition and attempts.
evidence: World state and run state contracts are tested.
Kernel happy path returns a world-state artifact ref and emits events.
gaps: No unified live agent attempt ledger.
No durable state manager coordinating all modules.
No runtime resumption policy across arbitrary work.
modules.next_checkpoint: Define a single state-manager contract that composes world state, run state, event ledger, and task plan state.

modules.name: Context manager
modules.requested_definition: Decides what information should be included in the model's context window.
modules.summary: UAA has context packs, grounded recall selection, context-pack building, context budget accounting, trimming, safe context proposal, and handoff approval contracts. It does not inject context into a live model session.
evidence: Recall and context-pack builders select safe summaries and enforce token limits.
Context handoff tests keep context injection disabled.
gaps: No runtime context-window manager for active model sessions.
modules.next_checkpoint: Promote from validated_contract only after a reviewed no-injection-to-injection boundary is designed.

modules.name: Memory module
modules.requested_definition: Stores, reviews, recalls, corrects, expires, and explains user/project/business memory without making memory authoritative.
modules.summary: UAA has governed memory records, write policy, local in-memory and SQLite-backed stores, source refs, provenance, recall metadata, redaction, retention/delete/export contracts, supersession, relationship/follow-up candidate schema, Founder Loop memory review storage, review-only decision metadata, and business-memory quality metadata. It is not yet the robust Founder Command Center memory advantage because cross-surface intake, memory write policy binding, retention/delete/export execution, context-injection policy, and full Today/Action/Evidence/Weekly Review binding are still planned.
evidence: M24 memory provider contracts and local stores are tested with source refs, review states, retention posture, redaction, and forbidden raw-content boundaries.
Founder Loop storage and relationship/follow-up candidate tests prove a bounded Memory Review substrate, not automatic memory authority.
UAA-P1-071 and UAA-P1-072 add review-only decision metadata plus safe-ref CRM-lite business-memory candidate and quality posture on the Today spine.
gaps: No cross-surface intake from local chat, local coding summaries, manual external-assistant review summaries, plans, actions, calendar/email metadata refs, and evidence timeline refs.
No memory write policy binding, retention/delete/export execution, or context-injection policy.
No mutation-capable quality-control actions for duplicate/conflict/stale records.
No completed Today/Action/Evidence/Weekly Review binding that makes reviewed memory feel like the full product spine.
modules.next_checkpoint: Use UAA-P1-073 through UAA-P1-077 to add reviewable Action envelopes, Chat/Code handoffs, cross-surface intake, and loop binding before raising maturity.

modules.name: Tool registry
modules.requested_definition: A standard way to define, describe, permission, and call tools.
modules.summary: UAA has ToolManifest, ToolRegistry, ToolBroker, capability firewall checks, consent and approval enforcement, and a governed tool runtime adapter with tightly allowlisted behavior. It deliberately does not support arbitrary tool dispatch.
evidence: ToolBroker evaluates registered tools against consent, risk, and capability firewall policy.
Runtime tests deny dynamic dispatch and preserve no-side-effect constraints for non-allowlisted paths.
modules.next_checkpoint: Keep arbitrary tools behind explicit capability registry, sandbox, approval, and audit milestones.

modules.name: Capability registry
modules.requested_definition: Lets the agent know what it can and cannot do.
modules.summary: UAA has a typed capability registry and coordinator lane with compact catalog disclosure, full manifest loading after selection, policy checks, exact approval validation, durable local state, telemetry, single-writer locking, adapter health checks, and tests. It is bounded to registered in-process capabilities and does not provide arbitrary runtime or external authority.
evidence: CapabilityManifest declares schemas, examples, anti-examples, risk, side effects, auth, context, runtime, safety, quality, and metadata.

Coordinator tests prove exact approvals, durable state, retries, idempotency denial, partial read failure artifacts, single-writer leases, adapter health checks, output-schema checks, and fan-out policy.
gaps: No external provider, browser, shell, plugin, or remote runtime authority from the registry itself.
Not all legacy modules consult the new registry yet.
modules.next_checkpoint: Bridge additional governed runtime adapters into the manifest lane without bypassing PolicyEngine, approval, state, and audit.

modules.name: Multi-agent coordinator
modules.requested_definition: Allows multiple specialized agents to work together.
modules.summary: UAA has a bounded local multi-agent coordinator that plans centrally, routes registered specialists as tools, supports handoff mode only by policy, supports read-only fan-out, serializes mutating work, records durable local state, validates approval grants, and returns structured artifacts. Remote dispatch, network coordination, and arbitrary agent spawning remain denied.
evidence: Coordinator tests prove planning, routing, structured task envelopes, read-only fan-out, parallel write denial, single-writer acceptance, exact approvals, durable state, failure artifacts, retries, adapter health checks, and output-schema validation.
A2A and remote-worker contracts remain inert metadata/dry-run boundaries, preserving no remote dispatch authority.
modules.next_checkpoint: Promote only after governed runtime integrations prove production auth, external adapter sandboxing, and operational rollout boundaries.

modules.name: Human-in-the-loop module
modules.requested_definition: Pauses the agent when approval, review, or clarification is needed.
modules.summary: UAA has local approval request/grant/validation logic, approval-bound tool/model route checks, review-only file approval contracts, and human checkpoint scheduling contracts. It can gate bounded local/dev paths, but it is not a general clarification or product approval workflow engine.
evidence: LocalApprovalAuthority creates, grants, revokes, and validates approval grants against exact scope.
Kernel and tool broker integration tests require valid approval for bounded high-risk local/dev actions.
gaps: No product-wide approval queue runtime as authority.
Human checkpoint scheduling is contract-only and does not schedule prompts or notifications.
modules.next_checkpoint: Unify approvals, clarification requests, and human checkpoints under one HITL decision surface before claiming operational_runtime.
